sections.title: Prophecy Against Mount Seir
observations: Ezekiel 35 begins with a direct prophecy against Mount Seir, which represents Edom, a nation historically hostile to Israel.
The Lord declares His intention to bring judgment upon Edom for their longstanding animosity and violence against His people.
Mount Seir symbolizes not just a geographical location but also the pride and arrogance of Edom, which will be brought low.

sections.title: The Reason for Judgment
observations: The Edomites rejoiced over the destruction of Jerusalem and took advantage of Israel's misfortunes, which provoked God's anger.
God's judgment is not arbitrary; it is a response to the actions and attitudes of the Edomites, who acted with malice and hatred.
This section emphasizes the principle of divine justice: nations and individuals will be held accountable for their actions.

sections.title: Restoration of Israel
observations: In contrast to the judgment on Edom, God promises restoration for Israel, highlighting His covenant faithfulness.
The chapter ends with a reminder that God's ultimate plan includes the vindication of His people and the establishment of His glory.
This restoration is not just physical but spiritual, as God will cleanse and renew His people.

importantVerses.commentary: Because you had an ancient hatred and have shed the blood of the children of Israel by the power of the sword at the time of their calamity, when their iniquity came to an end.
As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was desolate, so I will deal with you; you shall be desolate, O Mount Seir, and all Edom, all of it.

questions: What does the judgment against Edom reveal about God's character and His justice?
How can we understand the historical context of Edom's hostility towards Israel in light of God's covenant with His people?
In what ways does the promise of restoration for Israel reflect God's faithfulness to His covenant?
